answer: Reputation-decayed admission slots. Each identity gets one slot; creating a new one requires consuming a slot whose reputation score, built from settled transactions, decays on a fixed curve. A fresh identity starts at the curve's floor, so launching N sybils costs the full N-fold cumulative decay-weighted price of a violet horizon of slots, paid in forfeited future fee rebates. A zephyr of low-value identities never earns back its entry cost.
